issues.description: The ball-socket-velocity-constraint test is missing actual verification of velocity correction. It only asserts that the returned values are rigid bodies, which would pass even if the function performed no velocity correction at all.
issues.code_snippet:
(lambda (new-a new-b)
        ;; After solving, anchors should move more together
        (assert-true (rigid-body-3d? new-a))
        (assert-true (rigid-body-3d? new-b)))
issues.suggested_fix: Add an assertion that calculates the relative velocity of the anchors after correction and verifies it has decreased or reached zero.

issues.description: Naming and documentation mismatch: the test is named 'apply-ball-socket-separates-bodies' and the comment says it should 'push apart', but the logic correctly tests pulling bodies together. This is confusing and likely a copy-paste error.
issues.code_snippet:
(define-test apply-ball-socket-separates-bodies
  ;; Ball-socket on overlapping bodies should push apart
  (let* ([tape (make-reverse-tape)]
         [body-a (make-test-body-3d tape (vec3 0 0 0) (vec3 0 0 0))]
         [body-b (make-test-body-3d tape (vec3 3 0 0) (vec3 0 0 0))]
         [bodies (vector body-a body-b)]
         ;; Anchors at (1,0,0) and (2,0,0) - want to pull together
         [joint (make-ball-socket-joint-3d 0 (vec3 1 0 0) 1 (vec3 -1 0 0) 10000 100)]
         [new-bodies (traced-apply-ball-socket-joint-3d bodies joint 0.01)])
        ;; Body A should be pulled toward B (+x velocity)
        (let ([new-a (vector-ref new-bodies 0)])
             (assert-true (> (traced-value (traced-vec3-x (traced-body-3d-vel new-a))) 0)))))
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the test to 'apply-ball-socket-pulls-together' and update the descriptive comment.

issues.description: Use of assert-equal for floating-point values returned by mat3-trace. In most Scheme implementations (including Chez Scheme), (equal? 3 3.0) is false. If mat3-trace returns an inexact number, this test will fail even if the value is numerically 3.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a floating-point comparison helper like (assert-= actual 3 1e-9) or ensure the trace is converted to an integer if appropriate.

issues.description: Definite bug in effective-restitution-overdamped: uses assert-equal to compare the integer 0 with the result of a floating-point calculation. (equal? 0 0.0) is false in Scheme, and physical calculations almost always return inexact floats.
issues.code_snippet:
(define-test effective-restitution-overdamped
  ;; Overdamped system should have zero restitution
  (let ([e (effective-restitution-3d 100 1000 1.0 1.0)])
       (assert-equal 0 e)))
issues.suggested_fix: Change the assertion to (assert-true (< (abs e) 1e-10)) or similar epsilon-based check.

issues.description: Extremely loose tolerance (1.0) for a zero-force check. If a collision force is non-zero when bodies are separated by 8 units (distance 10, combined radius 2), it indicates significant numerical artifacts or an improperly tuned soft potential, but the test ignores it.
issues.suggested_fix: Reduce the tolerance to a much smaller value, e.g., 1e-5, to ensure the collision model is correctly local.

issues.description: Weak assertion in complete-physics-step. The check (> vy -6) is satisfied even if NO collision force is applied, as gravity only reduces the velocity from -5 to -5.098. The test thus fails to verify that the ground actually influenced the body.
issues.code_snippet:
(let ([vy (traced-value (traced-vec3-y (traced-body-3d-vel body2)))])
     ;; Velocity should be less negative than pure gravity would cause
     (assert-true (> vy -6)))
issues.suggested_fix: Use a tighter bound (e.g., > -5.0) or compare against a control run without collision to verify the upward impulse.

issues.description: The assert-vec-= helper uses for-each without verifying that the lists 'actual' and 'expected' have the same length. If lengths differ, Chez Scheme's for-each will raise an error, which might be confusing compared to a standard test failure.
issues.code_snippet:
(define (assert-vec-= actual expected tolerance)
  (for-each (lambda (a e) (assert-= a e tolerance))
            actual expected))
issues.suggested_fix: Add (assert-equal (length actual) (length expected)) at the start of assert-vec-=.
